articles.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals’ accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development.
articles.body_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.” “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.” The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.” “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.” But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power. Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software. Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.” Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research. In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.” “As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote. The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

articles.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The password manager maker said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate account and took some information about customers.
articles.body_text: Password manager maker 1Password has confirmed that some customer information was taken in a recent intrusion into its internal systems, but that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed. The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code. The attacker used that employee’s access to push malicious code to the company’s internal servers, which allowed the hacker to download some data about 1Password customers, including their names and the email address that they use for logging into their account. The company said that the attacker also took details about when a 1Password account was created and when a user last logged in. 1Password said that customer vaults, which store their passwords, were “at no point” available to the attacker. The company also said that it doesn’t have access to customer account passwords or their secret keys, which are used to scramble their passwords so that 1Password cannot see them. In addition, the company said that its apps and extensions are unaffected by the incident. It’s unclear how the attacker gained access to the employee’s corporate account, and a spokesperson for 1Password did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the incident. 1Password did not say whether it had notified customers whose information was taken in the breach, or how many customers had information taken. We’ve also asked if the company has received any communication or demands from the hackers. We’ll update if we hear back from 1Password. The company touts millions of customers and more than 200,000 businesses who use its password manager products to store their passwords, credentials, payment card information, and more. Security experts have long recommended password managers as a better way of generating stronger credentials and keeping track of online accounts. articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
articles.body_text: Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas. Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping. The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys. Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media. When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.” When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics. The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem , Lovi , Meemo Bear , BubblePal Panda , and Tavlshero ‘s AI Puppy . The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules. While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study. Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors. It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January , finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns. While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

articles.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: U.S. prosecutors accused the former executive of defrauding victims of ransomware by paying the hackers, charging victims more, and pocketing the difference.
articles.body_text: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back. According to federal prosecutors , Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.” But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement. Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida. The DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers. 404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count. Palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies. Last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they said they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks. The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal. articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.
articles.body_text: What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt ? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder. Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users. The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases , claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said. Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted . It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats. In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through. “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement. Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model. “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said . “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.” Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.” The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff .) Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google , when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The company also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform. California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

articles.title: Insta360’s new Ace Pro 2 has a bigger screen and AI-enhanced video recording.
articles.summary: Insta360’s new Ace Pro 2 features a larger, brighter screen, 8K video recording capabilities, and is powered by a pair of chips, improving its low-light recording capabilities.
articles.body_text: Insta360 has announced its new Ace Pro 2 action camera, an upgraded version of its GoPro Hero-series competitor. The compact camera now has a larger screen on the back that flips up 180 degrees for framing selfie videos, and it debuts at $399.99 — $50 cheaper than Insta360’s original Ace Pro. The design of the Ace Pro 2 still closely resembles the GoPro Hero series and DJI’s Osmo Action line, with an offset lens making room for an additional screen on the front. But while the front screen on the cameras of Insta360’s competitors can display full-color video, the Ace Pro 2’s monochromatic front screen only displays information. [Image: The front screen on the Ace Pro 2 is still limited to showing information, not video. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25691858/insta360_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] That’s why the company is carrying forward the hinged screen from the original Ace Pro and has bumped its size from 2.42 inches to 2.5 inches (matching the screen size of the recently announced Osmo Action 5 Pro), while also improving its brightness and pixel density. A larger screen makes it easier to frame shots, whether you’re standing in front of or behind the camera. However, that hinge is also a durability risk depending on what you’re using the Ace Pro 2 for. The other feature that distinguishes Insta360’s new action cam from the competition is its 8K capabilities. The Ace Pro 2 can now record 8K video at 30fps — a slight bump from 8K at 24fps previously — using what Insta360 describes as a “next-gen” version of the 1/1.3-inch image sensor from the original Ace Pro that’s paired with a 157-degree wide-angle Leica Summarit lens. Still photography is also boosted to 50MP. Dropping the camera’s resolution down to 4K boosts frame rates to 120fps, or 60fps in HDR, while 1080p mode can record as high as 240fps for smooth slow-motion captures. Insta360 says the Ace Pro 2 is powered by a Pro Imaging Chip, handling “image processing and noise reduction,” as well as an AI chip running a “complex, custom-trained AI neural network,” powering a PureVideo recording mode. When recording at night or in places where the lighting is dim, the PureVideo mode can boost the brightness of a video while also enhancing details. The camera can also leverage its AI capabilities to automatically create edited clips featuring what it decides are the best moments in a video. [Image: An optional Dive Case accessory lets the Ace Pro 2 be used at depths of 197 feet. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25691860/insta360_3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Ace Pro 2’s waterproofing has been extended to 39 feet — six feet deeper than the original — or 197 feet when used with an optional Dive Case accessory. Insta360 has also added a new “wind guard” to the front of the camera to improve the quality of audio captured during high-speed activities but with a magnetic mount so it can be easily removed when recording in quieter situations. Other features include a larger 1,800mAh battery that Insta360 says is rated at 180 minutes but with video recording limited to 1080p at 24fps. In 8K mode, battery life will definitely be shorter than that. The Ace Pro 2 can also continually capture up to 120 seconds before a recording is started to reduce the chances of missing a shot, allows recordings to be paused without creating a new video file, and supports both hand gestures and voice commands for operating the camera from afar. What Insta360 didn’t announce today is an updated version of the Ace camera that debuted alongside the original Ace Pro. Its video capabilities were limited to 6K at 30fps, but it was $70 cheaper than the Pro. Had a new version of the Ace debuted with the same $50 price cut as the new Ace Pro 2, it would have potentially been a cheaper alternative to both the $349 Osmo Action 5 Pro and $399 GoPro Hero 13 Black while offering better video capture capabilities.

articles.title: On the cusp of 24/7 service, robotaxis face pleas and protest in San Francisco
articles.summary: Waymo and Cruise are poised to expand robotaxi service in San Francisco to 24/7 operation. But city officials are concerned about blocked traffic, and some residents are using orange cones in protest.
articles.body_text: On a recent Friday evening, a driverless car pulled up alongside an outdoor dining shed in the Mission district of San Francisco, put on its hazard lights, and waited. As traffic began to pile up behind the vehicle, a man smoking a cigarette outside a nearby bar rolled his eyes. “I don’t drive a car,” he grumbled, “so I don’t really care about these things.” Other residents of this hilly city by the bay are not so ambivalent about the coming onslaught of autonomous cars. The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is poised to vote this Thursday on whether to allow Cruise and Waymo, the two main companies with autonomous vehicles in San Francisco, to expand their paid ridehailing services to operate 24/7. Currently, the companies only offer limited service. A vote in favor of the companies would essentially give robotaxis full access to the peninsula and its residents. They would be able to operate similarly to Uber or Lyft — travel anywhere in the city, at any time of day, and charge money for the rides. The vote also represents “the most significant regulatory moment for autonomous vehicles in the US over the last/next 3 years,” said Reilly Brennan, general partner at venture capital firm Trucks. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24780669/1497019989.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] According to Brennan, a robotaxi’s service area is also its total addressable market, a term in corporate finance that usually describes how much possible revenue a company can make. “If CPUC says it cannot operate 24 hours per day, you effectively have a reduced total addressable market,” he said in an email. “That’s why this upcoming vote is so critical: we’ll find out if the most significant US state (by revenue) is giving a green, yellow or red light to AV robotaxi’s future.” City officials are praying for a red light, or at least a yellow one. For months, they have been pleading with the state to delay the vote, citing a spate of incidents in which autonomous vehicles have stopped traffic, blocked buses, or obstructed emergency vehicles. The city’s transit agency and fire and police department have all logged complaints with the CPUC, calling for the commission to reconsider the plan for 24/7 service. “They’re not ready for prime time,” San Francisco Fire Chief Jeanine Nicholson told the Los Angeles Times recently. The department has logged 66 incidents since May 2022 in which robotaxis have interfered with firetrucks, according to The Washington Post. Many incidents have gone viral: robotaxis blocking intersections, forcing bus passengers to get out and walk, driving over fire hoses. In May, body camera footage captured a cop wielding a road flare at a Cruise vehicle, barking at it to “stay” as if it were an unruly puppy. After a mass shooting in June that wounded nine people, a robotaxi blocked a lane of traffic in the Mission district, slowing down emergency vehicles. The state’s Department of Motor Vehicles has logged nearly 75 collisions involving autonomous vehicles this year, including one last May in which a Waymo vehicle ran over and killed a small dog. The vehicle was operating with a safety driver in the front seat. The companies have defended themselves, noting that they are in communication with city officials about ways to improve to avoid future incidents. They also note that no one has been seriously hurt or killed by an autonomous vehicle in San Francisco, while many people are killed every year by human-driven ones. Pedestrian deaths in the city, much like in the rest of the country, have ticked up each year. There were 20 pedestrians killed by drivers in 2017 and 39 in 2022, according to city data. But some residents aren’t taking the slow advance of robotaxi coverage lying down. An activist group calling itself Safe Street Rebel put out a call on social media for people to place orange traffic cones on the hoods of any robotaxi seen wandering the streets of San Francisco, which would effectively disable it. “Cruise & Waymo promise they’ll reduce traffic & collisions, but we know that’s not true,” the pseudonymous account wrote on Twitter last week. “They block busses & emergency vehicles, create more traffic, and are a surveillance nightmare.” [Media: https://twitter.com/SafeStreetRebel/status/1676695665278337024] Autonomous vehicles usually have more cameras on them than typical passenger vehicles. Police could request footage from those cameras to investigate crimes or to violate residents’ privacy, advocates say. Waymo has received some requests for camera footage from law enforcement agencies but says it generally requires a warrant or court order. The companies were quick to condemn the orange cone protest, with a Waymo spokesperson calling it “vandalism.” An unnamed Safe Street Rebel told us in a Twitter direct message that some of the AV companies have “threatened to call the cops on us.” And the San Francisco transit agency spoke out against “ANY actions that may increase the number of disabled AVs on San Francisco streets.” The spread of robotaxis is testing San Francisco’s desire to continue to play guinea pig to Silicon Valley’s futuristic experiments. “I do believe people are both fed up with heavily distracted human-piloted vehicles / driver distractions *and* also that there has been a public backlash against AV fleets in some cities,” Brennan said. “There is a public chorus for a better, safer experience in cities.” Update July 11 9:40AM ET: Updated to include reactions to the orange cone protest.

articles.title: White House announces 25 percent tariff on Chinese tech goods
articles.summary: Today, President Trump announced an aggressive new set of tariffs against China, specifically naming touchscreens, batteries, and electric motors. Experts fear the move may provoke a trade war.
articles.body_text: Today, President Trump announced an aggressive new set of tariffs against China, setting a 25 percent import tax on $50 billion worth of “industrially significant technologies” imported from China. In previous discussions, China has threatened to retaliate against such tariffs, stoking fears of a far-reaching and unpredictable trade war between the countries. US Customs and Border Protection is set to begin collecting the tariffs on July 6th. A list published by the White House details more than 1,000 specific products that will be affected by the tariffs. It includes a broad range of components used in electronics manufacturing, specifically naming touchscreens, batteries, and electric motors. General components like transistors are also named on the list as well as more specific components used in televisions, cameras, and radio receivers. Fiber optic cables are also on the list, although most fiber optic cable is manufactured by US companies. Notably, the list does not include cellphones or completed televisions. Today’s list is a revision of an earlier proposal that was published in April that removed 515 items and proposed an additional 284. According to the White House, the tariffs are targeted at China’s “Made in China 2025” initiative, which aims to promote high-tech manufacturing within the country. “The United States can no longer tolerate losing our technology and intellectual property through unfair economic practices,” the White House said in a statement. In a response issued last night, China’s ministry of commerce pledged to respond with tariffs of “the same scale and the same strength.” The White House statement also pledged to implement additional tariffs if China retaliated, sparking fears of an escalating trade war that could significantly limit trade between the two countries.

articles.title: S-teorin: Kristersson tillträder – och utlyser nyval
articles.summary: Baudin i internt mejl: Förbered er för extraval – om Kristersson vinner
articles.body_text: Socialdemokraterna förbereder sig för ett extraval om Ulf Kristersson får bilda regering. I ett internt mejl som Expressen tagit del av uppmanar partisekreteraren Tobias Baudin till höjd beredskap. ”Vi följer utvecklingen noga”, skriver han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Socialdemokraterna rustar för ett extraval. Det framgår av ett mejl som partisekreterare Tobias Baudin skickat till partidistrikten. I mejlet skriver S-toppen att den Kristerssonregering riksdagen ska rösta om på måndag kommer – om den röstas igenom – att ”ha svåra förutsättningar att samla majoritet i riksdagen för sina politiska förslag”. En sådan minoritetsregering samlar bara 136 mandat i riksdagen och är således beroende av stöd från andra partier för att driva igenom reformer och budgetar. Moderaterna har i flera opinionsundersökningar under hösten ökat rejält, och i veckan har de fått sitt högsta stöd på åtta år. På andra sidan finns Socialdemokraterna som i samma undersökningar backat sedan valet – det val som innebar partiets sämsta valresultat någonsin. Socialdemokraterna behöver mot bakgrund av det ” ta risken för ett extra val på stort allvar om en regering ledd av Ulf Kristersson tillträder ”, skriver Tobias Baudin i mejlet. Tobias Baudin skriver vidare att den socialdemokratiska partiledningen kommer hålla ”en nära dialog” med partidistrikten under de närmsta dagarna. Han säger också att partiets organisationer ute i landet behöver höja beredskapen. ” Jag skulle därför behöva er hjälp med att, i dialog med arbetarekommunerna, efterhöra hur den organisatoriska beredskapen för att med kort varsel genomföra en ny valrörelse ser ut i era partidistrikt. ”

articles.body_text: Tre sjömän omkom när ett fiskefartyg med en besättning på 17 personer hamnade i sjönöd utanför Islands kust på onsdagen. De övriga 14 räddades efter ett stort räddningspådrag, rapporterar isländska medier. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Fartyget befann sig cirka 100 kilometer utanför Islands östkust när kaptenen under sen eftermiddag utlyste nödläge. Besättningen uppges därefter ha övergett fartyget som höll på att sjunka. Tre av dem har nu bekräftats omkomna. Omkring klockan 21, lokal tid, ankom en helikopter till platsen tillsammans med fartyg. Efter en ungefär två timmar lång insats kunde besättningsmedlemmar plockas upp ur vattnet och föras till orten Egilsstadir, rapporterar det isländska public service-bolaget Rúv . Vädret uppges ha varit mycket hårt, med upp till tio meter höga vågor. Förutsättningarna för helikoptern beskrivs som extremt krävande och fartyget befann sig i en avlägsen del av havet. – Det är så långt bort man kan komma och helikoptern kunde helt enkelt inte flyga snabbare, säger Georg Kristinn Lárusson, generaldirektör vid isländska kustbevakningen, till tidningen Morgunbladid. Det är oklart exakt vad som orsakade olyckan och hur resterande besättning mår. Insatsen är avslutad. ”Mina tankar går till sjömännen i öst, deras nära och kära och alla de goda och modiga människor som nu arbetar för att rädda dem”, skrev Islands president Halla Tómasdóttir på sociala medier under kvällen. articles.summary: Centerpartiet blixtinkallar till möte. Vid lunchtid möts partitopparna för att diskutera vägvalet, enligt Expressens uppgifter.
articles.body_text: Vid lunchtid möts partitopparna för att diskutera vägvalet, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På torsdagen har Centerpartiets partistyrelse och riksdagsgrupp kallats in till ett extrainsatt möte. Mötet sker runt lunchtid på torsdagen. Expressens har tidigare rapporterat om att stödet för en högersväng ökar i partiet, och den bedömningen görs fortfarande av C-källor. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. • Centerledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist har profilerat sig som företagandets röst. • Samtidigt visar Expressens genomgång att flera av hennes investeringar slutat i kostbara konkurser - bland annat för skattebetalarna. • Mitt under regeringsförhandlingarna gick ett av hennes investeringar i konkurs efter en längre tids misskötsel av ekonomin. Två ledande företrädare i bolaget polisanmäls nu Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist har byggt sin offentliga profil som politiker och partiledare på meriter som företagare. Hon lyfter fram sin bakgrund som styrelseordförande, vd och entreprenör och säger att det är med den erfarenheten som hon vill utveckla Centerpartiets ”redan företagarvänliga politik”. Men i sin egen affärsverksamhet har hon i flera år haft stora motgångar. Så sent som en vecka före valet gick en av hennes investeringar förlorad. Den sjunde september ansökte det norska bolaget Dynamisk Helse AS om konkurs vid domstolen i Trondheim. Bolaget, med både svenska och norska kommuner som kunder, har under ett par år erbjudit en app för utbildning av vårdpersonal. Trots att mångmiljonbelopp i norska kronor pumpats in i affärsidén, bland annat från Elisabeth Thand Ringqvists bolag, kunde företaget aldrig stå på egna ben. – Intäkterna kom ju aldrig upp till den kritiska nivån så att de hade täckning för kostnader och utgifter, säger konkursförvaltaren Ronald Eriksen Brevik.

Kim Ju-Ae är dotter till Nordkoreas ledare Kim Jong-Un. Tonåringen följde nyligen med sin pappa vid ett besök i nya skidorten Samjiyon i landets norra delar. Men bilderna på Kim Ju-Ae när hon åkte skidor under besöket har väckt uppmärksamhet. Amerikanska utrikesdepartementet varnar för att hennes lyxiga skidutrustning verkar vara från ”europeiska skidmärken”, enligt SCMP. De ser därmed ut att utgöra brott mot FN-sanktioner som stadgar att det är förbjudet att leverera lyxvaror till Nordkorea. Det amerikanska utrikesdepartementet påminde i ett uttalande som publicerades på tisdagen att sanktioner från FN:s säkerhetsråd förpliktar alla medlemsstater att ”förhindra direkt eller indirekt leverans, försäljning eller överföring av lyxprodukter till Nordkorea”. Schweiziska Stockli och österrikiska Fischer, vars logotyper förekom på bilderna, hävdar att man inte har sålt utrustning till Nordkorea. Kim Ju-Aes vita jacka har kopplats till det franska lyxmärket Rossignol och hennes byxor till franska friluftsmärket Salomon, enligt sydkoreanska medier. FN började införa sanktioner mot Nordkorea 2006 på grund av landets kärnvapenprogram. articles.body_text: Centern står inför ett uppslitande vägval – där allt fler börjar luta högerut. Många drar paralleller till tidigare jobbiga processer som partiet tagit sig genom. – Jag tror att fler i Centerpartiet vill vara med och ta ansvar i knepiga lägen än de som inte vill det, säger en C-källa. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På måndag kan det bli klart med en ny regering, om Ulf Kristersson (M) lyckas få med sig Centerpartiet . – Sverige ska få en regering som har stöd i riksdagen och som för en politik förankrad i mitten. Och för att nå dit så är vi beredda att samtala med båda sidor, sa C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist efter samtal med talmannen på tisdagen. Förhandlingar mellan M, KD, L och C väntas pågå onsdag, torsdag och fredag. Kristersson själv åker dock på EU-toppmöte i Bryssel, och kommer därför inte att medverka i samtalen i slutet av veckan. Sent på tisdagskvällen höll Centerpartiet ett internt informationsmöte där partiledningen gav sin bild av läget. Där betonades att ingenting ännu är avgjort, men att det var tydligt att partiledningen nu bara ser två realistiska alternativ – en M-ledd regering eller ett extraval, kunde Expressen avslöja efter mötet. Det ska ha stått klart ett extraval skrämmer och att C räknar med att straffas av väljarna för att ha varit ”bråkigt”. Partisekreteraren Hannes Hervieu ska ha hänvisat till att opinionsmätningar visat att C-väljare motsätter sig ett extraval.
